references.text: God gives Jacob the name Israel for the first time after the struggle at Jabbok. Genesis 35:10 confirms and reaffirms this name change in Bethel.
God changes Abram's name to Abraham as a sign of the covenant—a clear parallel to God changing Jacob's name to Israel.
The Lord who gave Jacob the name Israel is mentioned here, a direct reference to the name change in Genesis 35:10.
Hosea refers to Jacob's struggle with the angel and his encounter with God at Bethel, linking together the events of Genesis 32 and 35.
The same event told in two phases: the struggle over the name (32:29) and the final confirmation of the new name (35:10).
The name change in the patriarchal period is theologically linked to God's eternal identity and promise of redemption for the people.
The use of both 'Jacob' and 'Israel' in the same vision emphasizes the transition from the old name to the new one.
A parallel event where God changes a patriarch's name (Sarai/Sarah) to mark a new phase in salvation history.
Prophetic use of the names 'Jacob' and 'Israel' as titles for God's chosen, based on His grace.
Prophetic expansion where 'Israel' becomes an actively chosen identity marker for believers in the future.
